title: Frontiers | From Synapses to Silicon: Theoretical Foundations and Neuromorphic Implementations of Biological Learning
summary: This Frontiers in Neuroscience Research Topic explores the translation of biological learning mechanisms into neuromorphic engineering. It covers theoretical frameworks like predictive coding, analog VLSI implementations, emerging non-volatile devices (memristors), and on-chip architectures for spike-based computation. The resource explicitly excludes purely biological or device-physics studies lacking a clear computing component.
tldr: A Frontiers Research Topic soliciting papers on translating synaptic plasticity theories into scalable neuromorphic hardware and algorithms, with an acceptance deadline of 2027-02-12.
evidence: This Research Topic solicits original research articles... that advance our mechanistic and implementational understanding of learning in neural systems.

Analog VLSI implementations... have demonstrated that key aspects of biological learning can be realized in silicon with orders-of-magnitude improvements in energy efficiency relative to conventional digital hardware.
